ownership_reason: Only the gold looks at individual bytes and decides, for each byte at or below the space character, whether it is one of the whitespace bytes; hops 1-4 hold the whole String or array and get back one boolean, which cannot be traced back to the byte that produced it, and no change of the input above the gold (trimming, another charset, a narrower range) turns an admitted NUL into a rejection. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling overload Base64.isBase64(byte[]) (the facade's original delegate) admits a byte only if it is a Base64 character or one of space, LF, CR and tab (Base64.isWhiteSpace); testIsArrayByteBase64 asserts that {0} and negative bytes are rejected, testIsUrlSafe that {' ', '\n', '\r', '\t'} is accepted, testNonBase64Test that '%' is rejected, and all pass; BaseNCodec.isWhiteSpace documents 'Whitespace is taken to mean: space, tab, CR, LF'; Base32.isBase32(byte[]) applies the same rule; the facade's own javadoc says the String must contain only valid characters within the Base64 alphabet, whitespace being treated as valid. The gold's javadoc promises whether the range holds valid Base64 data, which a range holding the NUL byte does not. A one-line edit above the gold that passes the existing tests either discards the gold's result (returning the intact byte[] overload), re-implements the gold's per-byte decision before it, or is fitted to the trigger (requiring a Base64 last byte, or replacing NUL) and breaks the documented contract on other input (isBase64("abc\n") false, or "\u0001" accepted).
